name: Direct Relief: medicines and grants for US safety-net clinics
beneficiaries_note: Our build: medicines and grants for US safety-net clinics and disaster recovery, all in the United States and its territories.
summary: In the US, Direct Relief gives donated medicines and supplies ($297m at wholesale value in the year to June 2025, much of it generics for chronic illness, naloxone and contraceptives) to about 2,000 health centres, free clinics and charitable pharmacies serving uninsured patients, and $37m in grants for clinics and disaster recovery (Los Angeles fires, Hurricanes Helene and Milton). The health they buy is priced at the US health system's cost per QALY at the margin ($104,000 in 2019 dollars, Vanness et al. 2021), raised by half for patients who would otherwise go without, and Direct Relief is credited with its own cash's share of the resources, the donated goods being the manufacturers'. The result, about 0.0014 years of healthy life per $1,000, is far below the site's median because health is bought at US prices: a year of healthy life costs about a hundred times more at the margin in the US than in the countries Direct Relief serves abroad. Both branches are discounted by the shared missing-data slider: nothing measures the health these medicines produce.

sections.title: Cost
sections.explainer: What the modelled program cost in the year the outcomes below are counted for, including its share of overhead. From audited financial statements or the annual report.

sections.title: Reach
sections.explainer: How many people, animals or meals the spending reached in the same year, as the charity reports it.

sections.title: Effect per unit
sections.explainer: What the intervention does for each unit reached, from the best available studies, before any adjustment.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Other outcomes, in this model's unit
sections.explainer: charityevals' standard step for outcomes in more than one unit (docs/normalization.md 2.6): each outcome is counted in its own unit (units of value for income and deaths, WELLBYs for life satisfaction, tonnes of CO₂e, chicken pain days) and put into this model's unit by its unit's conversion over this unit's, which the headline's conversion cancels. So each moves only with its own sliders, exactly as in a model of its own unit. The rows are fixed; don't edit them.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

rows.label: US programme spending in cash, fiscal 2025

source.title: Direct Relief and Affiliates, Report of Independent Auditors and Consolidated Financial Statements, June 30, 2025 and 2024 (Baker Tilly, audited)

rows.explainer: Direct Relief's own spending on its US programme in the year to 30 June 2025, the latest with audited accounts: grants, bought medicines, freight, warehousing and staff. The USA column, $402,371k, less donated goods distributed ($296,794k), expired donated stock written off ($52,595k) and donated freight ($346k). Donated goods enter the credit share instead (Convention 2).

rows.label: Total expenses in cash, fiscal 2025 (all programmes, administration and fundraising)
rows.explainer: The shared Direct Relief figure: total expenses less every non-cash item.

rows.label: Programme expenses in cash, fiscal 2025 (USA and international)
rows.explainer: The shared Direct Relief figure: programme expenses less the non-cash items.

rows.label: Overhead multiplier (total ÷ programme expenses, cash)
rows.explainer: Spreads management and fundraising over programmes in proportion to their cash cost.

rows.label: Cost of the US programme, including overhead
rows.explainer: Cash programme spending times the overhead multiplier.

rows.label: Patient-years of medicine delivered in the US (defined daily doses ÷ 365)
rows.explainer: The year's defined daily doses not sent abroad, over 365: reach as years of treatment, dispensed by about 2,000 US partners (annual report p. 16), mostly community health centres, free and charitable clinics and pharmacies.

rows.label: Cost per patient-year of medicine delivered
rows.explainer: Context: Direct Relief's cash per patient-year of medicine its US partners received.

rows.label: Years each patient-year of medicine covers
rows.explainer: One: reach is already counted in patient-years of treatment.

rows.label: Baseline death rate (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used: deaths averted are counted inside the health-system figure (cost per QALY at the margin, below), whose health includes years of life saved, so a separate death chain would count them twice.

rows.label: Mortality reduction (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used: deaths averted are counted inside the health-system figure (cost per QALY at the margin, below), whose health includes years of life saved, so a separate death chain would count them twice.

rows.label: Indirect deaths per direct death (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used: deaths averted are counted inside the health-system figure (cost per QALY at the margin, below), whose health includes years of life saved, so a separate death chain would count them twice.

rows.label: Deaths averted per patient-year outside the DALYs below (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: deaths are in the health-system figure, counted once.

rows.label: Share of deaths averted under five (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used: deaths averted are counted inside the health-system figure (cost per QALY at the margin, below), whose health includes years of life saved, so a separate death chain would count them twice. The template's value, kept so the age bands stay defined.

rows.label: Of deaths at five or older, share aged 5 to 14 (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used: deaths averted are counted inside the health-system figure (cost per QALY at the margin, below), whose health includes years of life saved, so a separate death chain would count them twice. The template's value.

rows.label: Of deaths at 15 or older, share aged 15 to 49 (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used: deaths averted are counted inside the health-system figure (cost per QALY at the margin, below), whose health includes years of life saved, so a separate death chain would count them twice. The template's value.

rows.label: Illness as a share of deaths' and income's value (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: illness is counted once, in the DALYs below (high-income-care.md).

rows.label: Stillbirths averted counted separately (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: any are inside the health-system figure, counted once.

rows.label: Later-life income gain (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: no income effect is modelled separately for treatment of chronic illness in adults.

rows.label: Years until the income gain (not used)
rows.explainer: Not used, as the income gain is zero; kept so the income rows stay defined.

rows.label: Years the long-term income gain lasts
rows.explainer: The shared figure; multiplied by a zero income gain here.

rows.label: Later-life income gain per person reached, present value
rows.explainer: Discounted at the shared rate; zero here, as the income gain is zero.

rows.label: Resource sharing within households (multiplier on an earner's gain)
rows.explainer: The shared figure; multiplied by a zero income gain here.

rows.label: What the clinics would otherwise pay for these products ÷ their wholesale value
rows.explainer: Safety-net clinics buy through the 340B programme, whose ceiling prices are at least 23.1% below the average manufacturer price for brand drugs and lower for generics, and patients get manufacturers' assistance programmes: wholesale acquisition cost overstates what the goods would cost the system that uses them. Our judgment, 0.6 (0.35 to 1).

rows.label: Medicines and supplies delivered in the US, at what the clinics would pay
rows.explainer: The donated goods at the clinics' price plus what Direct Relief bought (at cost).

rows.label: US health system's cost per QALY at the margin, 2019 dollars

source.title: Vanness, Lomas, Ahn (2021), A Health Opportunity Cost Threshold for Cost-Effectiveness Analysis in the United States, Annals of Internal Medicine 174(1):25-32
source.quote: implies a cost-effectiveness threshold of $104 000 per QALY (UI, $51 000 to $209 000 per QALY) in 2019 U.S. dollars

rows.explainer: The health opportunity cost of US health spending: what a marginal dollar buys in health, estimated from how rising premiums make people drop insurance and the health that costs them. A QALY gained counts as a DALY averted.

rows.label: US cost per DALY averted at the margin, 2025 dollars
rows.explainer: The 2019 figure in 2025 prices (Convention 8).

rows.label: Health gained per dollar of these medicines ÷ per marginal dollar of US health spending
rows.explainer: The threshold is the health lost when people lose insurance; the patients here are uninsured or underinsured people at free clinics and health centres who would otherwise go without some of these medicines, and some products are cheap and life-saving (481,000 doses of naloxone, annual report p. 33) (+). Against that, the mix follows what manufacturers give, and some of it replaces what the clinics would have bought anyway (−). Our judgment, 1.5 (0.7 to 3).

rows.label: DALYs averted per patient-year of medicine (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The medicines' value per patient-year over the US cost per DALY at the margin, times the need ratio; deaths and illness are both in it.

rows.label: Grants: health gained per dollar ÷ per marginal dollar of US health spending
rows.explainer: Grants to health centres and free clinics (care for the uninsured), recovery after the Los Angeles fires and Hurricanes Helene and Milton (mental health, mobile clinics, rental assistance), solar power for clinics, maternal care. Some is less directly health. Our judgment, 1 (0.4 to 2).

rows.label: Grants: DALYs averted (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: The grants over the US cost per DALY at the margin, times the need ratio.

rows.label: Medicines: DALYs averted (before adjustments)
rows.explainer: Patient-years times DALYs per patient-year.

rows.label: How far the threshold's health per dollar holds
rows.explainer: The threshold is a model estimate (insurance loss and the deaths it causes), with a wide interval; it is not measured for these medicines. 0.85 (0.6 to 1).

rows.label: Fit to these patients
rows.explainer: One: how these medicines and patients differ from the marginal insured patient is in the need ratio.

rows.label: Evidence adjustment
rows.explainer: Internal times external validity.

rows.label: Share of the outcome that wouldn't have happened without Direct Relief
rows.explainer: Uninsured patients can sometimes get medicines through manufacturers' patient-assistance programmes, Medicaid enrolment or the clinic's own 340B purchases, and other charities (Americares, Dispensary of Hope) supply clinics too; some grant-funded work would have found other funders. Our judgment, 0.5.

rows.label: Medicines: Direct Relief's share of the resources behind them
rows.formula: (program_spend - us_grants) * overhead_ratio / ((program_spend - us_grants) * overhead_ratio + us_donated_goods * us_price_ratio)
rows.explainer: Convention 2: Direct Relief's cash for sourcing, storing and shipping (its US programme less grants, with overhead) over that cash plus the donated goods at the clinics' price. The clinics' staff time is inside the cost per DALY at the margin.

rows.label: Grants: Direct Relief's share of the resources
rows.explainer: One: the grant buys care at the system's cost per DALY, every input included.

rows.label: Share of credit used (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Medicines: share dispensed to patients before they expire
rows.explainer: Direct Relief wrote off $52.6m of expired US stock (audited accounts p. 7), 18% of the donated goods it shipped in the US ($296.8m); some of what clinics receive also expires on their shelves. Our judgment, 0.85.

rows.label: Grants: share spent as planned
rows.explainer: Grants go to vetted partners with milestone reviews before later payments (audited accounts p. 14). Our judgment, 0.9.

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Direct Relief takes no government money; a donation neither displaces nor draws in other money much. 1.

rows.label: Years a gift waits before it is spent
rows.explainer: The shared Direct Relief figure (facts/direct_relief.json), read by both models.

rows.label: Years from shipment to use
rows.explainer: Domestic shipping to clinics takes days to weeks; our judgment, a tenth of a year.

rows.label: Half of the year over which a patient-year of medicine is taken
rows.explainer: The middle of the year of treatment.

rows.label: Discount for the wait
rows.explainer: The gift's wait, delivery and the middle of the year of treatment, discounted at the shared rate.

rows.label: Medicines: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: Thin (Convention 12): doses are counted, but the health they produce is a judgment through the system's cost per QALY, not measured for these patients.

rows.label: Grants: counted less where the outcome isn't measured
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome data for the grant-funded care.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Medicines: all adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * attribution_share_shared * implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * med_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The medicines branch's adjustments.

rows.label: Grants: all adjustments combined
rows.formula: evidence_adj * counterfactual_adj * grt_attribution_share * grt_implementation_adj * leverage_funging_adj * wait_discount * grt_missing_data_adj
rows.explainer: The grants branch's adjustments.

rows.label: All adjustments combined (outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches, for reading only.

rows.label: Treatment costs averted (none counted)
rows.explainer: Zero: this is treatment, and money the clinics save is already counted through the cost per DALY at the margin.

rows.label: Rebound effects (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: no immunity effect for these medicines, which treat rather than prevent.

rows.label: Investment of income (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: no income gain is modelled for these patients.

rows.label: Other benefits and harms not modelled
rows.explainer: Benefits: hurricane preparedness packs pre-positioned at clinics, cold-chain and solar-power support keeping clinics open in outages, money patients save (+). Harms: the disposal burden of short-dated stock at clinics (−). Net +5% (−10% to +15%).

rows.label: Benefits and harms not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: The rows above, summed: they add to the modelled value as one share.

rows.label: Deaths averted outside the DALYs (none)
rows.explainer: Zero, as deaths are in the DALYs.

rows.label: Value of a death averted (units of value)
rows.explainer: The site's one value of a death, by age band, times your value of a life (multiplied by zero deaths here).

rows.label: Units of value from deaths averted (none)
rows.explainer: Deaths times the value of a death, zero here.

rows.label: Units of value from stillbirths (none)
rows.explainer: Zero stillbirths counted separately.

rows.label: Units of value from later-life income (none)
rows.explainer: Zero income gain.

rows.label: Units of value from illness, as a share (none)
rows.explainer: Zero: illness is in the DALYs.

rows.label: DALYs averted, both branches, after adjustments
rows.explainer: Medicines and grants, each with its own adjustments.

rows.label: Illness averted, in units of value
rows.explainer: DALYs into units of value at the shared rate (docs/normalization.md 2.6).

rows.label: Total units of value
rows.explainer: Every outcome in units of value, side effects at the shared weight.

rows.label: Units of value per dollar
rows.explainer: Outcome over cost.

rows.label: Staff's share of the cash cost
rows.explainer: Convention 1: Direct Relief's pay and benefits over its cash expenses.

rows.label: How much less staff earn than they could elsewhere
rows.explainer: The shared figure for staff of a delivery organisation.

rows.label: Salary forgone by staff (in-kind donation)
rows.explainer: Counted with credit by share of resources.

rows.explainer: Your dollar's share of the full cost.

rows.explainer: The headline, in units of value per dollar.
